query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_quality
per_column.rationale: Cabin crew is a plausible driver of Overall Rating and the categorical distillation (poor/good/exceptional/mixed) gives a groupable axis, though it partly overlaps the original 'Staff Service' numeric column. Samples 1,3,4,5 are well-read from the text. Sample 2, however, labels crew 'poor' when the review discusses only seats and the entertainment system and never mentions crew at all — an invented negative where the text is silent.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Ground service is a genuinely new axis absent from the original columns and useful for explaining satisfaction. It correctly returns Unknown for silent rows (samples 2–5). But sample 1 asserts 'smooth_efficient' for a review entirely about the onboard experience with no ground-service content — a confident specific not supported by the text.

per_column.name: food_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: Overlaps the original 'Food & Beverages' rating but adds finer categories (special_meal_failure, out_of_stock) that give some extra leverage. Samples 1,3,4 are correctly praised. Sample 2 labels food 'poor' though food is never mentioned, and sample 5 assigns 'adequate' to a review with no food content — both assert signal where the source is silent.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: Disruption handling is a distinct, high-value driver dimension not captured by any original column. All five samples correctly resolve to 'not_applicable' since none mention disruptions, showing sound handling of silent rows.

per_column.name: post_flight_service_outcome
per_column.rationale: Complaint-resolution outcome is a separate, meaningful axis for satisfaction. All sampled rows are appropriately 'not_applicable' with no post-flight content, correctly avoiding invented values.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Trivially redundant with the existing 'Value For Money' original column — a categorical restatement of the same construct, adding little new analytical leverage. Values are plausible and can be grounded in the existing numeric rating / overall sentiment, so groundedness is moderate.

per_column.name: service_consistency_trend
per_column.rationale: A temporal 'trend' (declining/improving/stable) is hard to derive from a single review; only sample 5 has explicit 'consistently good' support. Samples 1 and 2 receive 'stable_positive'/'stable_average' with no evidence of any across-time comparison, so the label is largely interpretive/invented rather than read from the text.

judge.rationale: The set provides several genuinely new axes for explaining Overall Rating — ground_service, disruption_handling, post_flight_service, and cabin_crew — which are the strongest contributions. value_for_money_perception is trivially redundant with the original 'Value For Money' column, and service_consistency_trend is a weakly grounded interpretive construct. Groundedness is mixed: disruption and post-flight columns correctly mark silent rows as not_applicable, but several columns (cabin_crew in sample 2, ground_service in sample 1, food in samples 2 and 5) confidently assert specific quality signals for aspects the review never discusses, and the trend column infers time-based movement from single reviews. This systematic tendency to manufacture values for silent aspects is the main groundedness concern.
